findings.message: Step 2c spawns infosec-reviewer but never says what to do when the agent errors or writes no `security/<TASK_ID>.md`. Plan 3c and verify 3.52 both record `NOT RUN — <reason>`; build is the third copy and drops it (B1: the NOT RUN handling covers two of the three call sites). Fix: when the agent errors or the file has no `**Verdict:**` line, write `security/<TASK_ID>.md` with verdict `NOT_RUN` and the reason, or append a NOT RUN line to the task report, so verify can tell 'not reviewed' from 'not an entry point'.
findings.scenario: Flag on. T4 adds a /login route. The infosec-reviewer spawn fails with a timeout. No security/T4.md is written and nothing is logged. At verify, the agent reads the security/ notes, finds none for T4, and the per-task review reads as if T4 were never in scope rather than unreviewed.

findings.message: The `expect` file has two parsers. The structural test pulls the rule and keyword with `[A-Za-z0-9]*` sed patterns. The runner (run-infosec-evals.sh:87) takes the whole rest of the line, strips spaces and uses it as a regex alternation. A malformed expect passes the structural check while the runner builds a regex that can never match. Fix: parse `expect` in one place, or make the structural test reject any line that is not exactly `rule: <ID>|<Keyword>`.
findings.scenario: expect = `rule: B16, Codes`. Structural test: rule=B16 (found), kw empty (check skipped) → PASS. Runner: want=`B16,Codes` → grep `\b(B16,Codes)\b` never matches → nightly catch rate 0% for a case the agent catches.

findings.message: `claude -p` is called with no timeout. A stalled call blocks the loop forever when run locally. In CI it blocks until the 60-minute job kill, and every later case goes unmeasured. Fix: wrap the call in `timeout <n>`. A timeout already exits non-zero, so the existing `|| return 0` counts it as 'no answer'.
findings.scenario: A network stall on the 2nd rep of case 3 → the runner never returns. Locally it hangs indefinitely. Nightly, the job is killed at 60 min, the result file has a partial table and no rates, and cases 4–8 are never measured.

findings.message: The 'fixed' sample still breaks the timing clause of the rule its case tests. A new account pays an argon2 hash; an existing one pays a mail send instead, so response timing differs. code-in-response/fixed.js:3 has the same gap: an unknown user returns 204 at once, a known one waits for a DB write and a mail. B18 is minor, so a correct WARN does not count as a false alarm, but the 'fixed' reference teaches the wrong fix. Fix: do equivalent work on both branches, or queue both off the request path.

The 'fixed' cap is check-then-act. It reads `saved.failures`, compares, then calls `recordFailure`. Parallel guesses all read the same count, so far more than MAX_ATTEMPTS can be tried. Fix: make the increment atomic and check the returned count, so the reference sample really caps attempts.
